 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Back in the 1980s, load management wasn't even a thing; NBA superstars and players couldn't imagine doing it. No matter how tired, bruised, and battered their bodies were, everyone took pride in stepping onto the court and putting on a show for the audience, both in the arena and for those watching at home on TV.
 When it came to putting on a spectacular show, no NBA team did it better than the "Showtime" Los Angeles Lakers. With the incomparable Magic Johnson running the show, fans got flashy passes and thunderous slam dunks nightly. Yet nobody can deny that the grind of an 82-game regular season still got to the players.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Former Lakers wingman Byron Scott , though, recalled how Magic found a crafty way to hit two birds with one stone: he got to regale fans with his play while still getting some rest.
 Magic studied the schedule
 Magic was savvy, not just with his passes, but in how he approached the game. Aware of his status and the clamor to see him, he didn't want to let the fans down. Byron revealed that Magic often looked at the schedule and circled some dates; these were games he felt they needed to dominate early so he and the rest of the starters could sit out the fourth quarter and rest.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Magic Johnson, he look at the schedule, and we warming up. He would come to us before the game start, 'Hey, man. Fourth quarter, I want to be sitting on the bench getting some ice," Scott said .
 Magic meant no disrespect to his opponents, but he knew how great his Lakers team was and which opponents they could blow out as early as the first half if they put their minds to it.
 "He would say, 'I want to be up by 25, 30 points, so in the fourth quarter we don't play. We can sit there and ice,'" Scott continued. "And that was our mentality on teams that we're supposed to beat." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "And that's that killer instinct that we're talking about that you got to have." 
 Related: "You're a millionaire, he's a billionaire. I'm going with him" – Magic Johnson on defying Lakers teammates to befriend Jerry Buss 
 Magic confirmed this tactic
 Magic himself confirmed this tactic . In a separate interview, he remembered telling his teammates to lock in and get the job done early.
 "I used to come into the locker room and tell the dudes, 'I don't want to play after the third quarter. I want to be sitting on the bench in the fourth quarter," the 6'9″ point guard revealed. "So, let's go out here, put the show on, and have ice on our knees in the fourth quarter." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "And what would happen? We'd go out there, bust them, blow them out, and in the fourth quarter — we'd be resting." 
 A win-win situation for everyone
 Magic's approach actually benefited everyone. Most starters got their numbers and rested long before the final buzzer, while fans got the show they paid hard-earned money to see. Most of all, the Lakers' second- and third-stringers got minutes they normally wouldn't get when the Lakers leaned on their core.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In other words, everybody went home happy.
